question.worked_solution:
The "square of a sum" formula states that

$$
{x}^{2}+2ax+{a}^{2}=(x+a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
{x}^{2}+\frac{3}{2}x+\frac{9}{16}.
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+\frac{3}{2}x+{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2\cdot \frac{3}{4}x+{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of sum formula with $a=\frac{3}{4}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x+\frac{3}{4})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
